nodes.name: NiCo PBA precipitation
nodes.procedure: 0.6 mmol nickel acetate and 0.9 mmol trisodium citrate dihydrate were dissolved in 20 mL of deionized water to form solution A. 0.4 mmol potassium hexacyanocobaltate(III) was dissolved in 20 mL of DI water to form solution B. Then, solution B was added into solution A under magnetic stirring. After continuous stirring for 1 min, the obtained mixed solution was aged at room temperature for 24 h. The precipitates were collected by centrifugation, washed with DI water and ethanol, and dried at 70°C in an oven overnight to obtain the final material (denoted as NiCo PBA).

nodes.name: Crystalline Ni(OH)2 hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: 20 mmol nickel(II) nitrate hexahydrate was first dissolved in 40 mL of deionized water. A 40 mL portion of 2M NaOH aqueous solution was then quickly added to the above solution under stirring to form a mixture. The mixture was then transferred to a 100 mL autoclave and kept at 160°C for 6 h. After cooling down to room temperature, the green precipitate was separated by centrifugation, washed with DI water, and dried under vacuum at 60°C overnight to obtain the sample of the layered crystalline Ni(OH)2.

nodes.name: Surface reconstruction in alkaline media
nodes.procedure: The prepared NiCo PBA electrode was immersed in a 1 M KOH solution for 1 h at room temperature to conduct surface reconstruction. After soaking NiCo PBA in 1 M KOH, distinguished reconstruction occurs on its surface where smooth surface becomes rough composed of nanosheet structures with lattice fringe spacing of 0.240 nm corresponding to (101) plane of Ni(OH)2 with low crystallinity.

nodes.source_text: When 20 mM HMF is introduced into the electrolyte, the current density on the Ni-Co PBA electrode increases dramatically starting from the potential of 1.40 V and reaches 70.6 mA cm⁻² at 1.55 V... A high HMF conversion of 96% is achieved over the NiCo PBA electrode, while the Ni(OH)₂ electrode only exhibits a HMF conversion of 80%. In addition, the selectivity to FDCA is as high as 99% for NiCo PBA... the Faradaic efficiencies for FDCA production over NiCo PBA and Ni(OH)₂ are around 95 and 67%, respectively. Remarkably, the TOF of NiCo PBA is calculated to be 17.84 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM images show nanosheet structures with lattice fringe spacing of 0.240 nm corresponding to (101) plane of Ni(OH)2 for NiCo PBA after soaking in 1M KOH; interplanar spacing expands slightly to 0.247 nm after potential application.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Lattice fringe with a spacing of 0.240 nm is measured on the nanosheet from the HRTEM image (Figure 1a inset), corresponding to the (101) interplanar spacing of Ni(OH)2... A slightly expanded interplanar spacing (0.247 nm) of lattice fringe is observed (Figure 1b).

nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in SEM and TEM in Figure S1a, the obtained NiCo PBA displays a uniform nanocubic structure with a smooth surface.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pristine NiCo PBA indexed to cubic Ni3[Co(CN)6]2·12H2O (JCPDS 89-3738); after KOH soaking transforms to low crystallinity Ni(OH)2·0.75H2O while as-synthesized Ni(OH)2 shows high crystallinity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD pattern in Figure S2a shows that all of the diffraction peaks can be indexed to the typical cubic Ni3[Co(CN)6]2·12H2O structure (JCPDS no. 89-3738)... Figure 1g shows the XRD patterns of NiCo PBA soaked in KOH and as-synthesized Ni(OH)2.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pristine NiCo PBA: Ni 2p at 856.46 eV (Ni²⁺), Co 2p at 781.76 eV (Co³⁺); after potential: NiCo PBA-derived Ni(OH)2 Ni³⁺ increases from 38.3% to 63.6%, crystalline Ni(OH)2 reaches 35.4%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The peaks at the binding energies of 856.46 eV for Ni 2p and 781.76 eV for Co 2p can be attributed to Ni²⁺ and Co³⁺... when a potential is applied, the percentage of Ni³⁺ on the NiCo PBA-derived Ni(OH)2 is increased from 38.3 to 63.6% (Figure 1h).

nodes.characterization_summary: PBA-derived Ni(OH)2 after KOH soaking: O 1s→Ni 3d eg transition peak at 533.5 eV (negative shift 1.4 eV vs crystalline Ni(OH)2 at 534.9 eV), indicating higher Ni valence state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: This transition peak energy of NiCo PBA after soaking in KOH (533.5 eV) shows a more negative shift of 1.4 eV than that of Ni(OH)2 (534.9 eV), indicating the existence of higher valence of Ni.

nodes.characterization_summary: PBA-derived Ni(OH)2 after KOH soaking shows pre-edge shift to higher energy and highest white line intensity vs crystalline Ni(OH)2, indicating increased Ni oxidation state and modified Ni-O environment.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the pre-edge position of Ni K-edge in NiCo PBA after soaking in KOH has a distinct shift to higher energy compared with other catalysts... the highest intensity and adsorption energy of white line peak... demonstrate an increase in Ni-oxidation state.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni-O coordination number 6.6 for PBA-derived Ni(OH)2 (after KOH) vs 5.3 for crystalline Ni(OH)2, indicating cation vacancies/defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The fitting results (Table S1 and Figure S6) show that the coordination number of Ni-O for NiCo PBA after soaking in KOH is 6.6, obviously higher than that for Ni(OH)2 (5.3).

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando Raman: NiOOH from PBA-derived Ni(OH)2 shows eg bending at 472.8 cm⁻¹ and A1g stretching at 553.8 cm⁻¹ for Ni³⁺-O; negative shift vs crystalline Ni(OH)2 indicates higher Ni³⁺ valence and more cation defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: two peaks at 472.8 and 553.8 cm⁻¹ appear obviously, which are attributed to the eg bending (δ) and the A1g stretching vibration (ν) mode of Ni³⁺-O, respectively... Raman spectra (Figure 1i) show that the NiCo PBA-derived catalyst exhibits a negative shift...
